idiom_name: async trait CustomerDao over sqlx (query_as with FromRow, no DSL)
implementation_notes: Rust has the interface machinery (traits) but essentially no standard-library persistence, so a DAO rides a library: sqlx is the async SQL toolkit with compile-time checked queries and no DSL, which makes a trait-per-aggregate natural - the trait is the DAO contract, the struct holding a pool is one implementation, and a second store or a mock is just another type implementing the same trait. What the language adds for free is boundary discipline: results are owned values inside Result<_, E>, so no cursor or connection handle can escape by accident. Keep the trait when implementations must be interchangeable; with a single concrete store a struct with an inherent impl is simpler.
pitfalls: sqlx errors are store errors: translate them into your own error enum at the trait boundary, otherwise PgDatabaseError and friends leak into business code.
Async traits and Send bounds interact with the pool: a DAO holding a borrowed connection cannot be shared across tasks, so hold the pool (PgPool/SqlitePool) and check out per operation.
fetch_optional versus fetch_one changes semantics - 'no rows' is Ok(None) in one and RowNotFound in the other - so picking the wrong one silently turns a normal miss into an error.

variants.name: Diesel typed-query DAO over a generated schema module
variants.idiom_name: diesel table! schema + Queryable/Selectable structs and load/first
variants.implementation_notes: Diesel takes the other route: schema.rs is generated from the database by the CLI, models derive Queryable/Selectable with the table name attached, and the DAO owns the connection and composes typed queries that are checked at compile time. Choose it when a blocking, DSL-style access layer with migrations already in place fits the application; choose sqlx when the runtime is async or when literal SQL should stay visible in the code. Trade-off versus sqlx is the schema module and migration tooling becoming part of the build.
pitfalls: PgConnection is not Sync and is not a pool: a connection-owning DAO cannot be shared across threads, so hand out pooled connections per call in a server.
schema.rs and the model structs drift from the real database unless migrations run through the Diesel CLI, and the compile-time checks then happily validate the wrong schema.
